newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses down sharply, hit by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses down sharply, hit by Wall St.

text.p: European bourses closed sharply down on Wednesday as Wall Street was hit by profit-taking with American investors jittery about the direction of interest rates.
And on currency markets, the dollar ran out of steam against the mark after earlier strengthening on growing speculation about a U.S. rate hike.
European equity markets had a disappointing trading session after an unsettled day on Tuesday when the bourses backtracked after roaring to new record trading highs.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, closed down by 0.5 percent, unsettled by Wall Street's negative opening. It was the London market's first setback in more than a week.
The FTSE index, having surged 137 points, or 3.2 percent, to record peaks during the previous six sessions, ended 21.8 points lower at 4,422.5.

"The market has run too far over the short term, but we're optimistic over the medium term," said NatWest equity strategist David McBain, whose year end target for the benchmark index is 4,600, the top of the range of forecasts.

European bourses, all trading at record levels in the last few days, seemed to lose their nerve as Wall Street fell at the start. American investors, worried about interest rates, trod cautiously ahead of this month's meeting of the Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee.
"We are taking a siesta as well we should. We have run about 640 points on the Dow so far this year," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards & Sons.
"The excuse for the time out is (Fed chairman Alan) Greenspan's verbiage. Has he cleared the way for a rate hike or hasn't he? We'll have choppy trade until the meeting"
In Paris, stocks ended the day with losses of 1.65 percent, weighed down by worries about long-term interest rate trends that fuelled profit-taking, traders said.

"A lot of analysts are unclear where the market's going from here," said Olivier Blitz at IFF Bourse. The bourse's underlying upward trend looked intact, particularly if the futures contract held above 2,670 points. If it broke that level, he said, a significant correction might take place.
In Frankfurt, shares on the computerised IBIS index closed 1.42 percent down because of the weakening dollar and the poor opening on Wall Street.

Floor trading had earlier closed showing losses of 1.31 percent. The market was weakened as chemicals group Hoechst AG fell 3.25 marks, more than four percent, to 71.95 after it shelved plans to list its HMR Marion Roussel unit.

On the currency front, the dollar slipped against the mark in late trading after remarks by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, who reiterated a statement made by Group of Seven finance ministers in Berlin last month that the dollar's correction from record lows in 1995 had been completed.
French finance minister Jean Arthuis echoed Tietmeyer's views by saying that current exchange rate levels should be consolidated.
But in a market hungry for further clues about the strength of the U.S. economy and their implications for interest rates, the comments caused only kneejerk selling, analysts said.

"The dollar is well supported by fundamentals and likely to remain fairly rangebound until at least later in the week when major U.S. data come out," said Sharda Persaud, international economist at San Paolo Bank here.

Attention is focusing on the next meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on March 25 amid speculation about whether the U.S. will raise interest rates. The next piece of economic data will be the Fed's Beige Book at 1900 GMT.
The Swiss franc staged a recovery despite fresh reassurances from France and Germany after bilateral talks that European monetary union will start on time.
Tietmeyer and Arthuis also reaffirmed the commitment of Germany and France to meeting the Maastricht criteria and sticking to the timetable for launching the euro in 1999.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.6960 marks and 122.50 yen compared with 1.7038 marks and 121.82 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 21.8 points at 4,422.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 44.45 points at 2,641.70.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index finished down 45.19 points at 3,415.40.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $352.65 an ounce, compared to $351.40 at the close on Tuesday. Silver was at $5.24 in late trade, up three cents. ($ = 5.760 French Franc)
